newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua transport workers threaten national strike.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua transport workers threaten national strike.

text.p: Nicaraguan transport cooperatives backed by the leftist Sandinista Front on Thursday threatened to launch a nationwide bus, truck and taxi strike to protest a new law that eliminated many tax breaks.
"We're going to have a national stoppage because it's the only way the government understands," Vidal Almendares, leader of one taxi federation, told reporters.
Luis Jimenez Roa, president of the Federation of United Transport Workers, said his group would wait to see the National Assembly's next move before deciding whether to strike.
Jimenez said his group represented 95 percent of the nation's bus, truck and taxi cooperatives.

A stoppage could revive the street protests that rocked the capital of Managua a month ago, especially because former President Daniel Ortega, leader of the opposition Sandinista party, threw his support behind the transport workers.
In the past the Sandinistas used their alliance with many of the largest transport cooperatives, combining strikes with protests, to pressure the government.

Deputies in the National Assembly, which is dominated by an alliance backing President Arnoldo Aleman, on Wednesday began approving key provisions of a law aimed at boosting this poor Central American country's anaemic tax base. That session continued on Thursday.

It took a truce between Aleman and Ortega to put an end to the Sandinista-led street protests and partial transport stoppage in April. The two leaders agreed to set up "working roundtables" between the government and the Sandinista party to cover a wide range of issues, but those sessions failed to produce an agreement on the tax law.
